narrative:
The model determined that you have a 45% chance of being a bad credit risk. Because this probability is high enough for the bank to consider you too risky, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that mattered most in this decision were your credit history, the status of your checking account, and the length of the loan you requested. Your credit history had the strongest influence and pushed the decision toward denial. You have no previous credits or have paid everything off, which is very uncommon. Only 1% of approved applicants share this profile, while most approved borrowers have a solid record of existing paid credits. This lack of proven credit behavior raised significant concern.

Your checking account status was the second most important factor and also worked against you. An account balance between 0 and 200 DM is less common among successful applicants. The bank prefers to see either no checking account at all or much higher balances.

The one positive element was the shorter 12-month duration you requested. Most approved loans average 19 months, so your shorter term helped reduce the risk in the model’s eyes. Unfortunately, this single favorable factor was not enough to overcome the concerns raised by your credit history and account status.

You should focus on building a stronger credit history by taking out and successfully repaying small loans or credit cards over time. Once you have established a positive track record, your chances of approval should improve. Consider reapplying after six to twelve months of responsible credit use.
